{{Use dmy dates|date=May 2023}} {{Short description|Indian educational technology company}} {{Infobox company | name = Educomp Solutions Limited | logo = Educomp logo.jpg | native_name = एडुकॉम्प सॉल्यूशंस | native_name_lang = hi | type = Public company | traded_as = {{BSE|532696}}
{{NSE|EDUCOMP}} | industry = [[Educational technology]] | founded = {{Start date and age|1994|09|07}} | founder = Shantanu Prakash | hq_location = 514 Udyog Vihar Phase III, [[Gurgaon]], Haryana 122001 | hq_location_country = India | area_served = Worldwide | website = {{URL|www.educomp.com/}} }} '''Educomp Solutions Limited (ESL)''' is an Indian [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[educational technology]] company, headquartered in [[Gurgaon]], Haryana, India. Founded in 1994 as a [[private limited company]] by Shantanu Prakash, it has offices across 18 [[States and union territories of India|Indian states]] besides having overseas presence in Singapore and the United States. The company was popular for its flagship product Educomp Smartclass{{Cite news|last=Saraswathy|first=M.|date=25 December 2013|title=Education firms learn a few lessons|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/management/education-firms-learn-a-few-lessons-113122500675_1.html|access-date=2022-01-11}} which once served thousands of schools in India, United States, Canada, Singapore and [[Sri Lanka]]{{Cite web|title=Educomp launches new interactive classroom programme|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/?from=mdr|access-date=2022-01-11|website=The Economic Times|language=en}} before the brand's acquisition by [[Ebix]] in 2018.{{Cite web|title=Educomp's Insolvency Process Becomes Murkier as Ebix Buys Smartclass Educational Services|url=https://thewire.in/business/educomps-insolvency-process-becomes-murkier-as-ebix-buys-smartclass-educational-services|access-date=2022-01-11|website=The Wire}}{{Cite web|title=Ebix forays into Indian edtech space with $8m majority stake in Smartclass|url=https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/ebix-smartclass-edtech-96506/|access-date=2022-01-11|website=DealStreetAsia|language=en-US}}{{Cite news|last1=Bhalla|first1=Mohit|last2=Khosla|first2=Varuni|title=Ebix leads the race to buy Educomp with Rs 325-crore bankruptcy offer|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/services/education/ebix-leads-the-race-to-buy-educomp-with-rs-325-crore-bankruptcy-offer/articleshow/62876492.cms|access-date=2022-01-11}} It was once described as India's largest technology-driven education company by ''[[The Economic Times]]''.{{Cite news|last=Chatterjee|first=Paramita|title=One good school of thought|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/services/education/one-good-school-of-thought/articleshow/2609701.cms|access-date=2022-02-01}} == History == Educomp Solutions Limited was founded as a [[private limited company]] by Shantanu Prakash, an alumnus of [[Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad]] and [[Shri Ram College of Commerce]] in September 1994.{{Cite news|title=Educomp Solutions Ltd.|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/company/educomp-sol-26839/information/company-history|access-date=2022-01-11}} The organization was engaged the business of setting up and maintaining of [[computer lab]]s in private schools under the [[Build–operate–transfer|BOOT model]] and in government-run schools under subcontracts awarded by [[Government of India|Indian government]] undertakings.{{Cite web|title=Educomp Solutions History {{!}} Educomp Solutions Information|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/educomp-solutions-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-17739.cms|access-date=2022-01-11|website=The Economic Times|language=en}} The company launched eCampus and PlanetVidya.com in 1998.{{Cite web|title=History of Educomp Solutions Ltd., Company|url=https://www.goodreturns.in/company/educomp-solutions/history.html#1641839400|access-date=2022-01-11|website=Goodreturn|language=en}} In 2000, the company started its trading operations with [[CD-ROM]]s. In September 2000, the firm was converted into a [[public limited company]]. In October 2000, the company received a US$2.5 million strategic investment from [[The Carlyle Group]].{{Cite news|title=Education biz's moving places|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/brand-equity/marketing/education-bizs-moving-places/articleshow/1212916.cms|access-date=2022-01-11}} The company entered the India's [[e-learning]] market in 2002 by launching LearningMate in partnership with US-based [[educational technology]] company [[Blackboard Inc.|Blackboard Inc]].{{Cite news|date=6 May 2002|title=Educomp ties up with US co for e-learning solutions|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/educomp-ties-up-with-us-co-for-e-learning-solutions/articleshow/9066078.cms|access-date=2022-01-11}} In June 2003, it launched Educomp Smartclass,{{Cite web|title=Educomp Solutions Ltd|url=https://www.edelbusiness.in/maruvayaparpaidhee-CUG/stocks/Educomp-Solutions-Ltd/company-history/26839.html|access-date=2022-01-11|website=www.edelbusiness.in|archive-date=11 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111163931/https://www.edelbusiness.in/maruvayaparpaidhee-CUG/stocks/Educomp-Solutions-Ltd/company-history/26839.html|url-status=dead}} a hardware for digitally equipping classrooms. In August 2004, it entered the American market by signing a US pilot project with [[Santa Barbara, California|Santa Barbara]]-based Franklin Elementary School.{{Cite web|author=Staff Reporter|date=14 February 2010|title=Educomp Solutions: Learn & Earn!|url=https://rakesh-jhunjhunwala.in/educomp-solutions-strong-growth/|access-date=2022-01-11|website=Rakesh Jhunjhunwala|language=en-US}} In 2005, Educomp was conferred the "CNBC-ICICI Bank Emerging India Award" as the ‘Company of the year 2005’ in the ICE and ITeS category.{{Cite web|last=Network|first=digitalLEARNING|date=3 August 2007|title=Set to Hit the One Billion Turnover by 2010 : Shantanu Prakash, CEO Educomp Solutions|url=https://digitallearning.eletsonline.com/2007/08/set-to-hit-the-one-billion-turnover-by-2010-shantanu-prakash-ceo-educomp-solutions-2/|access-date=2022-01-11|website=digitalLEARNING Magazine|language=en}} In 2008, it acquired 51% stake in Takshila Management Services. The company was on the height of its success between the years 2008 and 2012.{{Cite news|last1=Bhalla|first1=Mohit|last2=Basu|first2=Sreeradha D.|last3=Khosla|first3=Varuni|title=Educomp: Cautionary tale of a sudden fall from a star business to a bankrupt firm|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/services/education/educomp-cautionary-tale-of-a-sudden-fall-from-a-star-business-to-a-bankrupt-firm/articleshow/64008950.cms|access-date=2022-01-11}} In 2013, the firm signed a memorandum of understanding with Singapore's [[Raffles Institution]].{{Cite news|last=Reporter|first=B. S.|date=4 October 2007|title=Educomp signs MoU with S'pore-based Raffles|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/technology/educomp-signs-mou-with-s-pore-based-raffles-107100400041_1.html|access-date=2022-01-11}} In July 2016, ESL announced a joint venture called Ebix Educomp Solutions in which ESL held 49% stake, while the remaining 51% stake is held by Ebix Software. In May 2017, the company filed for insolvency in [[National Company Law Tribunal]].{{Cite news|last=Gairola|first=Manoj|date=6 April 2018|title=How Educomp may have subverted the spirit of India's IBC process|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/how-educomp-may-have-subverted-the-spirit-of-india-s-ibc-process-118040600049_1.html|access-date=2022-01-12}} In January 2018, Educomp launched an e-learning platform, SmartclassOnline.{{Cite web|last=Pandey|first=Navadha|title=Educomp launches e-learning platform|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/education/educomp-launches-elearning-platform/article7018660.ece|access-date=2022-01-11|website=@businessline|language=en}} In April 2018, [[Ebix]] purchased a majority stake of US$8 million for Smartclass Educational Services Pvt. Ltd (SESPL),{{Cite web|last=Varun|date=3 May 2018|title=US-based Ebix emerges as highest bidder for Educomp, also to acquire major stake in Smartclass Educational|url=https://www.theindianwire.com/startups/ebix-highest-bidder-educomp-55099/|access-date=2022-01-11|website=The Indian Wire|language=en-GB}}{{Cite news|last=ANI|date=1 May 2018|title=E-learning: Ebix to acquire majority stake in SmartClass Educational|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/e-learning-ebix-to-acquire-majority-stake-in-smartclass-educational-118050100184_1.html|access-date=2022-01-11}} thus paving the way for the former to enter India's 30 billion dollar digital education market.{{Cite web|last=Akash|date=1 May 2018|title=Ebix to enter India's $30 billion digital education market|url=https://digitallearning.eletsonline.com/2018/05/ebix-to-enter-indias-30-billion-digital-education-market/|access-date=2022-01-11|website=digitalLEARNING Magazine|language=en}} In May 2018, the [[International Finance Corporation]] submitted a petition to the [[National Company Law Tribunal]] asking to probe Educomp's alleged 'preferential transactions' after the company filed for bankruptcy.{{Cite news|last=Bhalla|first=Mohit|title=Educomp Bankruptcy: World Bank arm seeks independent investigation into Educomp bankruptcy|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/services/education/world-bank-arm-seeks-independent-investigation-into-educomp-bankruptcy/articleshow/64088000.cms|access-date=2022-01-12}} In June 2021, the [[State Bank of India]] filed a criminal complaint with the [[Central Bureau of Investigation]] accusing former director [[Rajat Khare]] of [[Appin (company)|Appin]] and others of embezzling ₹8.06 billion ($97 million) from loans to Educomp.{{Cite news |last1=Satter |first1=Raphael |last2=Siddiqui |first2=Zeba |last3=Bing |first3=Chris |date=2023-11-16 |title=How an Indian startup hacked the world |url=https://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/usa-hackers-appin/ |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=Reuters |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2021-06-29 |title=Central Bureau of Investigation First Information Report against Rajat Khare and Others |url=https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/23458565-20210629-central-bureau-of-investigation-fir-against-rajat-khare-and-others/ |access-date=2025-01-05 |website=DocumentCloud |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2015-03-20 |title=Rajat Khare's directorship at Educomp |url=https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/23458753-20160527-rajat-khare-resigns-as-director-of-educomp/ |access-date=2025-01-05 |website=DocumentCloud |language=en}} In September 2021, [[Supreme Court of India]] rejected Ebix's plea to withdraw its ₹4 billion offer for Educomp.{{Cite news|last=Bhalla|first=Mohit|title=Supreme Court rejects Ebix's plea to withdraw Rs 400 crore offer for Educomp|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/supreme-court-rejects-ebixs-plea-to-withdraw-rs-400-crore-offer-for-educomp/articleshow/86192813.cms|access-date=2022-01-11}} extract: Educomp Solutions Limited (ESL) is an Indian multinational educational technology company, headquartered in Gurgaon, Haryana, India. Founded in 1994 as a private limited company by Shantanu Prakash, it has offices across 18 Indian states besides having overseas presence in Singapore and the United States. The company was popular for its flagship product Educomp Smartclass which once served thousands of schools in India, United States, Canada, Singapore and Sri Lanka before the brand's acquisition by Ebix in 2018. It was once described as India's largest technology-driven education company by The Economic Times.
